..
Issued at 429 PM CDT Thu Sep 24 2026

Currently...

As expected, been a wet, dreary, cool day across the the
forecast area...with radar showing the main precipitation 
shield continuing to work its way northeast across the area, 
some southwestern areas already seeing a break in the rain. 
Thanks to it being an efficient rain, with precipitable water 
values exceeding 1.5 inches nosing into the region, area 
mesonets have shown a swath of 2-4 inches running roughly from 
Adams County southwest through Harlan County since midnight. 
Have held off on any formal hydro headlines up to this point, 
the overall rates/hours this rain is spread out over has been 
manageable...but this is an area especially that will have a 
close eye kept on it with the additional rain chances expected. 
Looking in the upper levels...data showing continued 
southwesterly flow in place across the region...set up between 
high pressure centered over the TX Gulf Coast region with its 
northward extending ridging, and troughing over the western 
CONUS driven by an area of low pressure over the Desert SW and 
another system approaching the coast of the Pac NW. A mid-upper 
level shortwave disturbance and increased lower level warm 
air/moisture advection is driving this ongoing 
precipitation...with the back edge of the more 
widespread/heavier rain working through WSWrn portions of the 
forecast area. Satellite imagery showing the area remaining 
socked in with low level stratus, with obs recording sub-1000 ft
ceilings. At the surface...the area sits between high pressure 
dominating much of the ENErn CONUS and a trough axis/frontal 
boundary draped through the western Plains...keeping winds 
southeasterly and generally on the lighter side of things around
10-15 MPH. Not surprisingly temperatures have struggled to do 
much today...sitting in the upper 50s to low 60s.

This evening through Friday night...

Main concern for this evening on through tomorrow night
continues to lie with precipitation chances. Models remain in 
good agreement in the broader picture, showing continued 
southwesterly flow in the upper levels...our precipitation 
chances driven by the passage of a couple more shortwave 
disturbances. After a bit of a lull from activity which moved in
last night...the next round of showers/storms is already 
working its way into the region from the southwest. Models 
continue to show this evening/overnight being the main timeframe
with this next batch...which they also show being more 
scattered in nature (vs the widespread shield of precip we had 
earlier in the day). Overall threat for severe weather is 
low...but instability isn't zero, not out of the question a few 
storms through tonight could produce some small hail/gusty 
winds. Of more concern would be additional rainfall...if any 
stronger storms with more notable rates were to spend much time 
over areas which already had 2- 4 inches of rain from earlier 
today, could have some minor flooding issues arise. 

During the daytime hours on Friday...in general models have
trended toward a less active period. Can't totally rule out 
precipitation for any particular portion of the forecast 
area...but the coverage appears that it'll be more isolated-
scattered in nature. Better chances look to arrive once again 
later in the day and more into the evening/overnight hours as 
lift increases with the arrival of the next upper level 
shortwave disturbance. Again the overall threat for severe 
weather is low (SPC Day 2 remains 'general thunder' for the 
area)...but if can get a few breaks in the clouds/better 
instability into the area, can't rule out some stronger storms.

This weekend on into the new work week...

Still some uncertainty with just how quickly precipitation exits
the forecast area off to the east on Saturday...some models 
have continued to trend a touch slower, potentially lingering 
activity across eastern areas well into the afternoon hours. 
Once the upper level trough driving those chances pushes east, 
models showing shortwave ridging working its way across the 
Plains...drying the forecast for Saturday night through at least
Sunday. It's possible that much of Monday ends up being dry as 
well...but do have some low chance PoPs in the forecast. Models 
showing the next notable upper level system arriving in the 
Tuesday-ish time frame...but uncertainties remain due to 
differences between models with how the system moves through. 
The ECMWF remains on the slower/stronger side with the potential
for more preciptiation...the GFS more progressive/quicker. 
Panning out like the ECMWF would drag precipitation chances 
further out into the rest of the week...GFS dries things out 
quicker. As far as temperatures go...still looking at 70s-low 
80s for the weekend-Mon...potentially more 60s Tuesday on, 
depending on how precip works out.
